summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of morbid obesity, chronic lymphedema, recurrent cellulitis, obstructive sleep apnea, and prior DVT/PE on warfarin was admitted for worsening right leg swelling, pain, and shortness of breath. She had recently completed a course of clindamycin for cellulitis. Imaging ruled out DVT but confirmed severe lymphedema. She was treated with IV vancomycin for presumed recurrent cellulitis, diuresis with furosemide and home diuretics, and pain management. During admission, she developed oral and suspected esophageal candidiasis, requiring a 14-day course of fluconazole, which necessitated warfarin dose reduction and strict INR monitoring. Her PICC line was successfully exchanged due to malposition. By discharge, infection and swelling had improved, INR was therapeutic, and she was stable for discharge home with services and detailed follow-up instructions.
problems: Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
